title: Stock sim gate: a 0.05 mm overcut of a bore is under the 0.625 mm lattice and gives 0 gouge cells

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found during #917 (PR B, the STEP import through solidcore).

## What we see

The pin `bore_facet_sagitta` cuts an MCP bore on `Milling-test.step` with an oversize radius `r + d`. The program-gate sim counts the gouge cells. Cell 0.625 mm, tol 0.01 mm on both builds:

| d (mm) | main (truck mesh) | #917 branch (solidcore mesh) |
|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | 2 cells, at (12.189, -2.813) | 0 |
| 0.1 | 10 | 8 |
| 0.3 | 34 | 32 |

## Cause

- At d 0.05 the overcut ring is r 12.50..12.55.
- On both lattices only 8 cell centres fall in that ring, all at r 12.507..12.509. That is within 0.01 mm of the true wall.
- The #299 lateral slack (tol 0.01) absolves exactly these cells, by law.
- Main convicted 2 cells only because the coarser truck chord put the mesh wall inside the slack ring (the same sagitta effect that #689 fixed on the nominal side). The main pin passed by chance.

## Why it is not a wrong output now

At d 0.05, verify still holds the post on the branch: `ok false`, `held_by` the operation, by the generator law "cuts past the finish surface". At d 0.1 and 0.3 the sim convicts the overcut.

## What to do

- Decide how the sim gate sees an overcut that is narrower than one lattice cell on a wall. Options: a finer local lattice near the part walls, or a judge on the wall distance of the swept tool, not on cell centres.
- Add a pin at d 0.05 that asserts the sim gate counts the overcut, when the option is chosen.
